COL1.d: Inferred: name of the MIB item described by the record. Unique in every release (105,222 distinct values in 105,222 rows of the 2025 release). Matches pcf.PCF_NAME (77,565 rows), cpc.CPC_PNAME (3,676), ccf.CCF_CNAME (2,221), txf.TXF_NUMBR (208), prf.PRF_NUMBR (77) and paf.PAF_NUMBR (52); 21,423 names match none of these tables in the same release.

COL2.d: Inferred: symbolic name of the item in the flight or instrument software (e.g. data-pool or ICD mnemonic). In 18,984 rows of the 2025 release it simply repeats COL1, apparently when no software name exists. Not unique: 102,326 distinct values for 105,222 rows, because one software item can correspond to several MIB items (e.g. 'ALU' maps to four parameters NIU00362, NIU003E5, PIU51141, PIU51181).

COL3.d: Inferred: free-text description of the item, often longer than the 24-character PCF_DESCR (e.g. 'Watchdog A status', or a full sentence for commands). Filled in 89,560 of 105,222 rows (2025). 2,729 rows contain only the placeholder 'a'. 23 values are exactly 255 characters long, which suggests truncation by the generating tool (inference).

CAF_NUMBR.d: Alphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the numerical calibration definition (calibration curve). It is the value used in PCF_CURTX, CUR_SELECT and CAP_NUMBR. Per the mcf and lgf remarks (p. 70-72), it must not coincide with any MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT, since all non-textual calibrations share one name space.

CAF_DESCR.d: Free textual description of the calibration curve.

CAF_ENGFMT.d: Format of the engineering values (CAP_YVALS) given in the cap records of this curve.

CAF_RAWFMT.d: Format of the raw values (CAP_XVALS) given in the cap records of this curve. It must be compatible with the type of the parameters that use the curve.

CAF_RADIX.d: Radix in which the raw values of the cap records are written. Only applicable to unsigned integer raw values (CAF_RAWFMT = 'U'); engineering values are always decimal.

CAF_UNIT.d: Engineering unit mnemonic of the curve, available for consistency checking against the unit (PCF_UNIT) of the parameters that use it. The row is shaded grey in the ICD (not used by SCOS-2000 processing).

CAF_NCURVE.d: Number of calibration points defined in cap for this curve. Grey row in the ICD: informative, not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CAF_INTER.d: Extrapolation behaviour for raw values that fall outside the range covered by the calibration points (CAP_XVALS). This is the flag SCOS-2000 actually uses (PCF_INTER is ignored), so all parameters that share the curve behave the same; if different behaviours are required, a copy of the curve with another flag has to be defined.

CAP_NUMBR.d: Identifier of the calibration curve this point belongs to; must match CAF_NUMBR of an existing caf record.

CAP_XVALS.d: Raw value of the calibration point, written in a format compatible with CAF_RAWFMT. Unsigned integer raw values (CAF_RAWFMT = 'U') must be written in the radix of the curve (CAF_RADIX).

CAP_YVALS.d: Engineering value of the calibration point, written in a format compatible with CAF_ENGFMT. All engineering values, including unsigned integers, are written in decimal whatever the curve's CAF_RADIX.

CCA_NUMBR.d: Alphanumeric name uniquely identifying the commanding numerical (de-)calibration curve; referenced by CPC_CCAREF, CSP_CCAREF and CCS_NUMBR.

CCA_ENGFMT.d: Numeric format of the engineering values given in the CCS records of the curve (CCS_XVALS). It must be compatible with the engineering format (CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT) of the parameters using the curve.

CCA_RAWFMT.d: Numeric format of the raw values given in the CCS records of the curve (CCS_YVALS). It must be compatible with the type (PTC) of the parameters using the curve.

CCA_RADIX.d: Radix in which the raw values (CCS_YVALS) of the curve are written; only applicable when the raw values are unsigned integers (CCA_RAWFMT=U). It may differ from the radix (CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX) of the parameters using the curve.

CCA_UNIT.d: Engineering unit mnemonic, provided for consistency checking against the unit (CPC_UNIT/CSP_UNIT) of the parameters using the curve. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CCA_NCURVE.d: Number of CCS records (points) defined for this curve. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CCF_CNAME.d: Unique name (mnemonic) of the command. It is the key referenced by CDF_CNAME (command structure), PTV_CNAME (pre-transmission validation), CVP_TASK (verification profile), PSM_NAME (parameter sets), CSS_ELEMID (use of the command in a sequence) and by the default values of command or sequence parameters of type 'Command ID'.

CCF_DESCR.d: Short textual description of the command, up to 24 characters, shown alongside the command name in SCOS-2000 displays.

CCF_DESCR2.d: Detailed description of the command, up to 64 characters. Printed with a grey background in ICD 7.0, meaning that SCOS-2000 does not use the field for any processing.

CCF_CTYPE.d: Command type. For missions following the Packet Telecommand Standard it flags special commands that are not ordinary TC packets. For control segments (R) and control frames (F) the PCDF/CDF entries of the command describe the frame data field instead of a packet header plus application data; the ICD strongly recommends giving BC frames (Unlock, Set V(R)) a global interlock (CCF_ILSCOPE='G') waitin

CCF_CRITICAL.d: Criticality flag. A critical (also called hazardous) command is flagged Y; the extra processing or protection applied to critical commands is left to mission-specific implementation.

CCF_PKTID.d: Name of the TC packet header (TCP_ID) used when constructing the command packet. The PCDF elements of that header decide which of CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID and CCF_ACK are needed.

CCF_TYPE.d: PUS service type of the command, an integer 0 to 255, copied into the header element of PCDF_TYPE 'T'. It may be empty if the selected packet header has no element of type T.

CCF_STYPE.d: PUS service subtype of the command, an integer 0 to 255, copied into the header element of PCDF_TYPE 'S'. It may be empty if the selected packet header has no element of type S.

CCF_APID.d: Application process identifier of the command, copied into the header element of PCDF_TYPE 'A'. Allowed range 0 to 2047 for spacecraft commands and 2048 to 65535 for non-spacecraft commands. It may be empty if the header has no element of type A. The APID also selects the routing defined in DST (commands whose APID is not in DST go to the NCTRS) and must be present whenever CCF_RAPID is set.

CCF_NPARS.d: Number of elements (parameters and fixed areas) of the command, provided so that the off-line database can check it against the number of CDF records of the command. Grey background in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CCF_PLAN.d: Identifies which external sources may reference this command directly in a planning file.

CCF_EXEC.d: Controls whether the command may be loaded on SCOS-2000 manual stacks on its own, or only as part of a command sequence.

CCF_ILSCOPE.d: Default interlock scope applied when the command is loaded on a SCOS-2000 command source, i.e. which commanding is blocked while the command waits for the verification stage given by CCF_ILSTAGE. The subsystem-based options use CCF_SUBSYS. A sequence element can override it with CSS_ILSCOPE.

CCF_ILSTAGE.d: Default verification stage that an interlock raised by this command waits for. Option O is handled as U when commanding in BD mode. The importer checks this field against the command verification profile: if a CEV stage (A or C) is requested but the command has no such stage in CVP/CVS, the importer replaces the value with the highest stage applicable to that command (A or O). A sequence element c

CCF_SUBSYS.d: Identifier of the subsystem the command belongs to, an integer 1 to 255. It is used by the subsystem-scoped interlock options (S, B, T), to derive the on-board subsystem mnemonic shown by TC SPACON for redundant APIDs, and as the default sub-schedule identifier when CCF_SUBSCHEDID is empty.

CCF_HIPRI.d: Flags a command implemented on board as high priority: its MAP ID is forced to the fixed value given in CCF_MAPID and it cannot be execution time-tagged on board (typically CPDU commands of a packet-based mission). High-priority commands cannot be aggregated, i.e. they cannot be part of a command block (see CSS_BLOCK).

CCF_MAPID.d: MAP identifier to be used for a high-priority command, an integer 0 to 63. Irrelevant unless CCF_HIPRI is Y.

CCF_DEFSET.d: Name of the parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) applied by default to the command parameters when the command is loaded.

CCF_RAPID.d: Redundant APID of the command, for redundant on-board units that accept the same command under a different APID. The TC SPACON application can dynamically force the use of the redundant APID for a selected prime APID; when this field is set, TC SPACON offers an entry showing the subsystem mnemonic (from CCF_SUBSYS) and the prime APID (CCF_APID), which must then also be set. Range 1 to 2047 (zero n

CCF_ACK.d: Default acknowledgement flags of the command: the decimal value (0 to 15) of the complete 4-bit Ack field of the packet data field header, copied into the header element of PCDF_TYPE 'K'. It may be empty if the header has no element of type K. Since R4.0 the flags can be changed when the command is loaded on a command source, which is also the way to disable dynamically a report-based verification

CCF_SUBSCHEDID.d: Identifier (1 to 65535) of the default on-board sub-schedule used when the command is loaded as an execution time-tagged command. If empty, the value of CCF_SUBSYS is used as default. A sequence can impose its own default with CSF_SUBSCHEDID. The ICD 7.0 text wraps the field name over two lines as 'CCF_SUBSCHED ID'.

CCS_NUMBR.d: Name (CCA_NUMBR) of the curve to which this value pair belongs.

CCS_XVALS.d: Engineering value of the point, in a format compatible with CCA_ENGFMT. All values, unsigned integers included, are written in decimal whatever the curve radix (CCA_RADIX). Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.

CCS_YVALS.d: Raw value of the point, in a format compatible with CCA_RAWFMT; unsigned integer raw values (CCA_RAWFMT=U) are written in the radix CCA_RADIX. Part of the key. Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.

CDF_CNAME.d: Name of the command (CCF_CNAME) to which the element belongs.

CDF_ELTYPE.d: Type of the command element. Only editable elements (E) may be given values in sequence definitions (SDF); the importer rejects SDF entries for fixed parameters.

CDF_DESCR.d: Textual description, used for fixed areas only (CDF_ELTYPE=A); parameters are described by CPC_DESCR.

CDF_ELLEN.d: Length of the element in bits. For fixed areas SCOS-2000 uses it to encode the command. For fixed or editable parameters SCOS-2000 ignores it, because the length follows from the PTC/PFC of the referenced parameter, but it should still be filled correctly so that the consistency of command and parameter definitions can be checked. It must be 0 for variable-length parameters (e.g. PTC=7, PFC=0).

CDF_BIT.d: Bit offset of the element counted from the start of the unexpanded application data field, i.e. just after the packet header (including the data field header where present, as defined in PCDF). Offsets of elements that follow a repeated group are computed as if every counter were 1. SCOS-2000 uses the offset only to sort the elements: they are encoded in that order with no gaps, not at the absolut

CDF_GRPSIZE.d: For a group repeater (counter) parameter, the number of following command elements that form the group to be repeated N times at load time, N being the counter value. For any other element it is left empty or 0. The field becomes part of the table key when it is non-zero. A group repeater with a fixed value and a non-zero group size is expanded automatically; a fixed counter with group size 0 is j

CDF_PNAME.d: Name of the command parameter (CPC_PNAME) placed at this position. It must be given for parameter elements (CDF_ELTYPE F or E) and is irrelevant for fixed areas (A).

CDF_INTER.d: Representation of the fixed or default value in CDF_VALUE, or the source of that value. Irrelevant for fixed areas.

CDF_VALUE.d: Fixed or default value of the element; its maximum length depends on the maximum command size (section 3.3.3.2). For a fixed area it is a raw unsigned integer written in hexadecimal, at most 32 bits (FFFF FFFF); fixed areas must not be used for Service 11 command elements that have to be processed for ground modelling (by the OBQM). Zero is a valid value for fixed areas and for group repeaters. Fo

CDF_TMID.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) whose current value provides the dynamic default; used only with CDF_INTER=T. Its PTC/PFC must be identical to those of the command parameter in CDF_PNAME, and only parameters processed by the telemetry model library qualify: TM parameters that appear in PLF, or synthetic parameters of any type.

CPC_PNAME.d: Unique name of the command parameter. CDF_PNAME refers to it to place the parameter in a command; SDF_PNAME and PVS_PNAME refer to it indirectly through the command definition.

CPC_DESCR.d: Textual description of the command parameter, up to 24 characters.

CPC_PTC.d: Parameter Type Code: identifies the raw type (unsigned integer, signed integer, real, octet string, character string, absolute time, relative time). The supported codes, their interpretation and the format in which raw values must be written are listed in Appendix A of the ICD (PDF p.214-220), which follows the PUS nomenclature with SCOS-2000 extensions (for example PTC=5/PFC=4 48-bit MIL-STD 1750

CPC_PFC.d: Parameter Format Code: together with CPC_PTC it determines the length of the parameter, and its range must be compatible with the PTC as listed in Appendix A. For 'Deduced' parameters (PTC=11) it controls the width: 0 means the width is taken from the associated TM parameter, a positive value forces the encoded width to that number of bits whatever the size of the TM parameter.

CPC_DISPFMT.d: Input and display format of engineering values, for calibrated parameters and for time parameters. The option must match the calibration category and, for numeric calibration, the engineering format of the referenced CCA curve. The value formats for each representation are given in Appendix A. Not used for 'Command ID' (CATEG=A), 'Parameter ID' (CATEG=P) and 'Deduced' (PTC=11) parameters.

CPC_RADIX.d: Default radix in which the raw value of an unsigned integer parameter is displayed. It may be overridden by a mission-configurable set of allowed radices. It also governs how raw unsigned values written in CPC_DEFVAL, CDF_VALUE and SDF_VALUE must be expressed.

CPC_UNIT.d: Engineering unit mnemonic (for example VOLT) displayed next to the parameter value. CCA_UNIT and PRF_UNIT are checked against it for consistency in the off-line database.

CPC_CATEG.d: Kind of calibration or special processing applied to the parameter. It must be empty or N for parameters whose raw value is not numeric (strings, times) unless they are 'Command ID' or 'Parameter ID' parameters, and it is not used for 'Deduced' parameters, whose calibration comes from the associated TM parameter. It determines which of CPC_CCAREF and CPC_PAFREF must be filled and whether engineeri

CPC_PRFREF.d: Name of the parameter range set (PRF_NUMBR) that restricts the allowed values of the parameter. The representation of the range set (PRF_DSPFMT) must be compatible with the parameter type: with CPC_PTC if the ranges are raw (PRF_INTER=R), or with CPC_DISPFMT if they are engineering. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.

CPC_CCAREF.d: Name of the numeric (de-)calibration curve (CCA_NUMBR) used to convert between engineering and raw values. The raw and engineering formats of the curve (CCA_RAWFMT, CCA_ENGFMT) must be compatible with CPC_PTC and CPC_DISPFMT. It must be empty if CPC_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or T, and must be filled if CPC_CATEG is C or B. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.

CPC_PAFREF.d: Name of the textual (de-)calibration, i.e. alias set (PAF_NUMBR), associated with the parameter; its aliases may also serve as default values. The raw format of the alias set (PAF_RAWFMT) must be compatible with CPC_PTC. It must be empty if CPC_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or C, and must be filled if CPC_CATEG is T or B. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.

CPC_INTER.d: Representation in which CPC_DEFVAL is written. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.

CPC_DEFVAL.d: Parameter-level default value, used whenever a CDF entry asks for it (CDF_INTER='D'); useful when the same default must apply to every instance of the parameter in every command. Its maximum length is not fixed but depends on the maximum command size (section 3.3.3.2). It must be written in the representation chosen by CPC_INTER: raw values in a format compatible with CPC_PTC (and CPC_RADIX for un

CPC_CORR.d: States whether an absolute time parameter is time-correlated, using the applicable time correlation coefficients, when its raw value is interpreted. For relative time parameters (PTC=10) it must be set explicitly to N. CPC_OBTID selects which on-board clock format and correlation apply; without correlation, the on-board time format must still be known to establish the time reference (the absolute

CPC_OBTID.d: Identifier of the on-board time (OBT) used to encode/interpret time parameters, either to apply the time correlation or to define the time format and in particular its epoch. The OBT ID is a SCOS-2000 configuration identifier for each on-board clock of the mission; with N clocks it takes values 1 to N. If not given, the mission default OBT ID set by the MISCconfig variable TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID is us

CPC_ENDIAN.d: Future extension (grey and italic in ICD 7.0, so not used by any SCOS-2000 version, as also stated by change S2K-7749). It is meant to give the byte order of parameters whose length is a whole number of octets; the conversion would be possible for signed and unsigned integers, strings, octet strings, absolute and relative times.

CPS_NAME.d: Name of a parameter set (PST_NAME). Part of the key.

CPS_PAR.d: Name of a command parameter (CDF_PNAME) or of a sequence formal parameter (CSP_FPNAME) that belongs to the set given in CPS_NAME.

CPS_BIT.d: Unique identification of the parameter within the set: for command parameters, its bit offset in the command (CDF_BIT); for sequence parameters, its position (CSP_FPNUM). Part of the key.

CSF_NAME.d: Unique name of the command sequence. Referenced by CSS_SQNAME, SDF_SQNAME and CSP_SQNAME (content of the sequence), by CSS_ELEMID when the sequence is nested in another one (CSS_TYPE=S), and by PSM_NAME and CVP_TASK.

CSF_DESC.d: Short textual description of the sequence.

CSF_DESC2.d: Detailed description of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CSF_IFTT.d: States whether the sequence (or any nested sequence) contains execution time-tagged commands, and therefore how the user is asked for times when loading it.

CSF_NFPARS.d: Number of formal parameters of the sequence, for consistency checking against the number of CSP records of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000.

CSF_ELEMS.d: Number of elements of the sequence, for consistency checking against the number of CSS records of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000.

CSF_CRITICAL.d: Criticality flag of the sequence; the additional protections for critical (hazardous) sequences are mission specific.

CSF_PLAN.d: Identifies which external sources may reference the sequence directly in a planning file.

CSF_EXEC.d: Controls whether the sequence may be loaded stand-alone on SCOS-2000 manual stacks or only as a nested sequence inside another sequence.

CSF_SUBSYS.d: Identifier of the subsystem the sequence belongs to, 1 to 255.

CSF_GENTIME.d: Time at which the sequence was generated. Grey: informative only.

CSF_DOCNAME.d: Name of the document (procedure) from which the sequence was generated. Grey: informative only.

CSF_ISSUE.d: Issue of that document. Grey: informative only.

CSF_DATE.d: Issue date of that document. Grey: informative only.

CSF_DEFSET.d: Name of the default parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) for the sequence.

CSF_SUBSCHEDID.d: Default on-board sub-schedule identifier (1 to 65535) used when the sequence is loaded as execution time-tagged. If set, every execution time-tagged command of the sequence is assigned this sub-schedule; if empty, each command keeps the default given by its own CCF_SUBSCHEDID.

CSP_SQNAME.d: Name of the sequence (CSF_NAME) owning the formal parameter.

CSP_FPNAME.d: Name of the formal parameter; unique within the sequence but not necessarily across sequences. Referenced by SDF_VALUE (VTYPE=F) of the same sequence, by SDF_PNAME when the sequence is nested, and by CSS_ELEMID for formal-parameter elements.

CSP_FPNUM.d: Number of the formal parameter within the sequence, used to order the parameters (and, for a nested sequence, quoted in SDF_POS). Numbers must be consecutive without gaps. Range 0 to 65535 as from R5.0; 0 to 999 in earlier releases.

CSP_DESCR.d: Textual description of the formal parameter.

CSP_PTC.d: Parameter Type Code (see Appendix A), with the same meaning as CPC_PTC. It must equal the PTC of every element parameter associated with this formal parameter.

CSP_PFC.d: Parameter Format Code, giving the length together with CSP_PTC within the ranges of Appendix A. It must equal the PFC of every associated element parameter.

CSP_DISPFMT.d: Input/display format of engineering values for calibrated and time parameters, as for CPC_DISPFMT. It must be equivalent to that of every associated element parameter, and is unused for 'Command ID' (CATEG=A) and 'Parameter ID' (CATEG=P) parameters.

CSP_RADIX.d: Default radix for displaying the raw value of an unsigned integer formal parameter; it may differ from the radix of the associated element parameters.

CSP_VTYPE.d: Representation of the default value CSP_DEFVAL. Must be filled for type P when a default is given, and must be empty for types C and S.

CSP_DEFVAL.d: Default value of the formal parameter; its maximum length depends on the maximum command size. For type P it is written as stated by CSP_VTYPE (raw compatible with CSP_PTC and CSP_RADIX, engineering compatible with CSP_DISPFMT). For 'Command ID' (CATEG=A) it names a fully defaulted command (CCF_CNAME); for 'Parameter ID' (CATEG=P) a monitoring parameter with an on-board identifier (PCF_PID). For t

CSP_CATEG.d: Calibration or special processing category, as CPC_CATEG. It must be empty or N for non-numeric raw types (strings, times) unless the parameter is a 'Command ID' or 'Parameter ID'. Options A and P are only allowed if every element parameter mapped to this formal parameter is of the same special type.

CSP_PRFREF.d: Name of the range set (PRF_NUMBR) checking the formal parameter value; its format (PRF_DSPFMT) must suit CSP_PTC or CSP_DISPFMT depending on PRF_INTER. Must be empty for types C and S. It need not be the range set of the associated element parameters, but a different set is only safe if it is more restrictive (all its values allowed for every associated element parameter). CSP_CCAREF.d: Name of the numeric (de-)calibration curve (CCA_NUMBR), compatible with CSP_PTC and CSP_DISPFMT. Must be empty if CSP_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or T, filled if C or B, empty for types C and S, and if filled it must be the same curve as used by every associated element parameter.

CSP_PAFREF.d: Name of the textual (de-)calibration (PAF_NUMBR), whose aliases may serve as values; its raw format must suit CSP_PTC. Must be empty if CSP_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or C, filled if T or B, empty for types C and S, and if filled the same as used by every associated element parameter.

CSP_UNIT.d: Engineering unit mnemonic displayed with the value; it should agree with the unit of every associated element parameter.

CSS_SQNAME.d: Name of the sequence (CSF_NAME) the element belongs to.

CSS_COMM.d: Free comment attached to the element; for elements of type T (textual comment) this is the text that command sources would display. The whole row is printed in italics in ICD 7.0, i.e. the field is not currently supported by SCOS-2000.

CSS_ENTRY.d: Entry number of the element, giving its position in the sequence. Entries must be consecutive (no gaps). Part of the key.

CSS_ELEMID.d: Identifier of the element: for type C a valid command name (CCF_CNAME), which ICD 7.0 says must not contain group repeater parameters (but see the SDF section, which since R4.2 allows commands with fully defined repeated groups); for type S a valid sequence name (CSF_NAME); for types F and P a formal parameter name (CSP_FPNAME) of this sequence; for type T it must be empty.

CSS_NPARS.d: Number of editable parameters of the element, i.e. the number of SDF records for this element; only relevant for elements of type C or S. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

CSS_MANDISP.d: Whether the command needs its own manual dispatch (ARM and GO) on a manual stack. Must be left empty for commands inside a group or block (CSS_GROUP or CSS_BLOCK = M or E) except the first command of the group/block. Irrelevant for non-command elements.

CSS_RELTYPE.d: Reference used with CSS_RELTIME to compute the command release time tag, or the release start time of a nested sequence.

CSS_RELTIME.d: Delta release time of the element, written as hh.mm.ss up to 23.59.59 (other separators such as ':' are accepted). For a command with RELTYPE=R and manual dispatch, the release time is the dispatch time plus this delta; for a command with RELTYPE=R without manual dispatch, it is the release time of the last command before it in the expanded top-level sequence (if the previous element is a nested s

CSS_EXTIME.d: Delta execution time tag of the element, written [+][ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] for positive and -[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] for negative intervals (other separators accepted). With PREVREL=R the execution time of a command (or the execution start of a nested sequence) is the execution time of the last execution time-tagged command before it in the expanded top-level sequence plus the delta; with PREVREL=A it

CSS_PREVREL.d: Reference used with CSS_EXTIME to compute the execution time tag of a command or the execution start time of a nested sequence.

CSS_GROUP.d: Grouping condition (commands only): grouped commands are released as one batch that cannot be interleaved with commands released by other command sources. A group has at least a start and an end command, with a configurable maximum number of middle commands; only the first command (S) may have a manual dispatch flag or a release time tag. Empty when the command is not grouped; irrelevant for non-c

CSS_BLOCK.d: Blocking condition (commands only): blocked commands are released in a single data unit by aggregating their packets into one segment data field. A block has at least a start and an end command, with a configurable maximum number of middle commands; a block may sit inside a group but not a group inside a block; only the first command may have a manual dispatch flag or release time tag. CSS_ILSCOPE.d: Interlock scope for this command element, overriding CCF_ILSCOPE. For commands inside a block or group, G and L are only allowed on the last command (E). If empty, the command definition applies. Irrelevant for non-command elements.

CSS_ILSTAGE.d: Verification stage that the interlock of this command element waits for, overriding CCF_ILSTAGE. O is handled as U in BD mode. The importer prevents requesting a CEV stage (A or C) not foreseen in the command's CVP/CVS profile and substitutes the highest applicable stage (A or O). If empty, the command definition applies.

CSS_DYNPTV.d: Whether the dynamic PTV checks (feasibility checks, time checks, interlocks) are overridden for this command element. Irrelevant for non-command elements.

CSS_STAPTV.d: Whether the static, telemetry-based PTV check (PTV table) is overridden for this command element. Irrelevant for non-command elements.

CSS_CEV.d: Whether the command execution verification (CEV) checks are disabled for this command element. Irrelevant for non-command elements.

CUR_PNAME.d: Name of the parameter to be calibrated; must match the PCF_NAME of an existing monitoring parameter (whose PCF_CURTX must then be left null).

CUR_POS.d: Evaluation order of the applicability criteria of the calibrations attached to the parameter, starting with the lowest value. Only the first calibration whose criterion CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR is true is activated; the other entries of the same parameter are ignored.

CUR_RLCHK.d: Name of the parameter whose value decides whether this calibration applies; CUR_VALPAR gives the value it is compared with. Only parameters with a signed or unsigned integer raw representation that are processed by the telemetry model library (TM parameters with a plf entry, or synthetic parameters of any kind) may be used.

CUR_VALPAR.d: Raw value of the applicability parameter CUR_RLCHK for which this calibration applies; the applicability expression is CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR.

CUR_SELECT.d: Identifier of the calibration to apply when the applicability expression is true. It must match TXF_NUMBR if CUR_PNAME is a status parameter (PCF_CATEG = 'S'), or CAF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT if it is numerical (PCF_CATEG = 'N'). All calibrations attached to the same parameter must give the same engineering format: ASCII for textual calibrations; real for polynomial, logarithmic and numerical

CVE_CVSID.d: Identifier (CVS_ID) of the verification stage this check belongs to. Only parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE = 'V') are allowed. Part of the key.

DPC_NUMBE.d: Name of the AND this record belongs to; must match DPF_NUMBE of an existing dpf record. Part of the table key together with DPC_FLDN.

DPC_NAME.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) shown at this position, or Null. When Null the record is a free entry: the text in DPC_TEXT is shown and DPC_COMM, DPC_MODE and DPC_FORM are not relevant. When a parameter name is given, DPC_TEXT is ignored. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model (TM parameters appearing in plf or synthetic parameters) may be used (§3.3.2.7, PDF p.110). The ICD

DPC_FLDN.d: Position of the parameter on the display, 0 to 63. Positions 0-31 are shown on the left side and 32-63 on the right side. Part of the key: a display position can hold only one entry.

DPC_MODE.d: Controls whether the Telemetry Desktop option governing the display of invalid parameter values applies to this entry.

DST_APID.d: Command APID to which the routing applies, an integer 0 to 65535 (so it covers both spacecraft APIDs 0 to 2047 and non-spacecraft APIDs 2048 to 65535). All commands with this CCF_APID use the route.

DST_ROUTE.d: Destination identifier: a string of up to three fields separated by dots. GPC_WHERE.d: Plot area where the parameter is drawn. GPC_NAME.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) plotted. Must be processed by the TM model (plf parameter or synthetic parameter, §3.3.2.7).

GPC_RAW.d: Selects whether calibrated or raw values are plotted. It also fixes the representation used for GPC_MINIM and GPC_MAXIM.

GPC_MINIM.d: Minimum value of the parameter, mapped to the start of the axis on which the value is projected. Expressed in raw or engineering form according to GPC_RAW, in a format compatible with the parameter type (Appendix A).

GPC_MAXIM.d: Maximum value of the parameter, mapped to the end of the axis. Raw or engineering form according to GPC_RAW, format per Appendix A.

GPC_PRCLR.d: Colour of the plot symbol and of the connecting lines.

GPC_SYMB0.d: Symbol drawn at each parameter value. The field name is printed with a final digit zero ('SYMB0') in the ICD text; the HPSDB note writes 'SYMBO'.

GPC_LINE.d: Line style connecting two consecutive values (two symbols).

GPC_DOMAIN.d: Identifier of the SCOS-2000 domain to which the plotted parameter (GPC_NAME) belongs, unsigned integer 0 to 2^16-1. GPF_NUMBE.d: Name of the Graphical Display (GRD): alphanumeric string that uniquely identifies it; referenced by gpc.GPC_NUMBE.

GPF_TYPE.d: Screen layout of the graphic display. The number of plots per screen portion is a maximum, currently 8 in total. The type also determines the allowed plot-area codes in GPC_WHERE.

GPF_HEAD.d: Alphanumeric header shown on the top line of the display.

GPF_SCROL.d: Controls whether the display scrolls when the plot reaches the end of the plot area(s). It has no meaning for parameters plotted against spin phase or against another parameter.

GPF_HCOPY.d: Controls the automatic hardcopy (print) when the end of the plot area is reached.

GPF_DAYS.d: Number of days in the X-axis time span; for parameter-against-parameter displays it sets the duration of the display. Integer 0 to 99.

GPF_HOURS.d: Number of hours in the X-axis time span (or display duration for parameter-against-parameter plots). Integer 0 to 23.

GPF_MINUT.d: Number of minutes in the X-axis time span (or display duration for parameter-against-parameter plots). Integer 0 to 59.

GPF_AXCLR.d: Colour of the axes, ticks and grids.

GPF_XTICK.d: Number of intervals between ticks on the X axis. Integer 1 to 99.

GPF_YTICK.d: Number of intervals between ticks on the Y axis. Integer 1 to 99.

GPF_XGRID.d: Number of intervals between grid lines on the X axis. Integer 1 to 99.

GPF_YGRID.d: Number of intervals between grid lines on the Y axis. Integer 1 to 99.

GPF_UPUN.d: Display update rate in seconds, integer 1 to 99. Provided for external applications that read the database; not used by SCOS-2000.

GRP_NAME.d: Unique identification name of the monitoring group; referenced by GRPA_GNAME and GRPK_GNAME.

GRP_DESCR.d: Textual description of the monitoring group (the ICD prints 'Textural'). Mandatory.

GRP_GTYPE.d: Type of the monitoring group, which decides whether its members are listed in grpa or grpk.

GRPA_GNAME.d: Name of the monitoring group to which the parameter belongs; must match GRP_NAME of a group with GRP_GTYPE = 'PA'.

GRPA_PANAME.d: Name of the parameter belonging to the group; must match PCF_NAME. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model library (TM parameters in plf, or synthetic parameters of any type) may be used.

GRPK_GNAME.d: Name of the monitoring group to which the packet belongs (the ICD's wording says 'parameter', copied from grpa); must match GRP_NAME of a group with GRP_GTYPE = 'PK'.

GRPK_PKSPID.d: SPID of the telemetry packet belonging to the group; unsigned integer matching PID_SPID.

LGF_IDENT.d: Alphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the logarithmic calibration; used in PCF_CURTX and CUR_SELECT. It must not overlap with CAF_NUMBR or MCF_IDENT values.

LGF_DESCR.d: Free textual description of the logarithmic calibration.

LGF_POL1.d: Coefficient A0, a numerical value in real format (Appendix A).

LGF_POL2.d: Coefficient A1 of the first-order logarithmic term ln(X), in real format; defaults to 0.

LGF_POL3.d: Coefficient A2 of the second-order term ln^2(X), in real format; defaults to 0.

LGF_POL4.d: Coefficient A3 of the third-order term ln^3(X), in real format; defaults to 0.

LGF_POL5.d: Coefficient A4 of the fourth-order term ln^4(X), in real format; defaults to 0.

MCF_IDENT.d: Alphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the polynomial calibration; used in PCF_CURTX and CUR_SELECT. It must not overlap with CAF_NUMBR or LGF_IDENT values.

MCF_DESCR.d: Free textual description of the polynomial calibration.

MCF_POL1.d: Coefficient A0 (constant term), a numerical value in real format (Appendix A).

MCF_POL2.d: Coefficient A1 of the first-order term, in real format; defaults to 0.

MCF_POL3.d: Coefficient A2 of the second-order term, in real format; defaults to 0.

MCF_POL4.d: Coefficient A3 of the third-order term, in real format; defaults to 0.

MCF_POL5.d: Coefficient A4 of the fourth-order term, in real format; defaults to 0.

OCF_NAME.d: Name of the parameter to be checked; must match PCF_NAME of an existing monitoring parameter.

OCF_NBCHCK.d: Number of consecutive valid samples of the parameter that must violate a check before the parameter is declared out of limits (OOL). It filters out isolated glitches. When the Behaviour Limit Checker optimisation is enabled, MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR must exceed the largest value used here (warning at the start of section 3.3.2.3.1, p. 73, which spells the field 'OCF_NBCHK').

OCF_NBOOL.d: Number of checks defined for this parameter in ocp, an integer from 1 to 16. It must be consistent with the number of ocp records for the parameter.

OCF_INTER.d: Whether the limit values OCP_LVALU and OCP_HVALU of this parameter are raw or engineering values. Option 'C' is allowed only for parameters with one or more calibrations (see PCF_CURTX and cur). OCF_CODIN must be compatible with the data type of the view chosen here, and if the parameter is used in a command verification expression (cve) OCF_CODIN must also be compatible with CVE_INTER.

OCF_CODIN.d: Data type in which the limit values OCP_LVALU and OCP_HVALU are written.

OCP_NAME.d: Name of the parameter to be checked; must match OCF_NAME of an ocf record (and therefore a PCF_NAME). For event checks it also forms the event ID 'BEHV::<OCP_NAME>'.

OCP_POS.d: Order in which the checks of the parameter are applied. The table is expected to be sorted by OCP_NAME and OCP_POS, with soft/hard pairs ordered soft first. OCP_HVALU.d: High limit value in the format given by OCF_CODIN (Appendix A). Relevant only for limit and delta checks of numerical parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'N'). For limit checks (OCP_TYPE 'S', 'H' or 'E') it is the high limit and cannot be null. For delta checks ('D') it is the maximum delta: it may be null (no maximum-delta check) and otherwise must be positive, applied in both directions. Irrelevant for stat

PAF_NUMBR.d: Alphanumeric name uniquely identifying the commanding textual (de-)calibration (alias set); referenced by CPC_PAFREF, CSP_PAFREF and PAS_NUMBR.

PAF_RAWFMT.d: Numeric format of the raw values (PAS_ALVAL) of the alias set; it must be compatible with the type of the parameters using the set.

PAF_NALIAS.d: Number of PAS records (aliases) defined for this set. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

PAS_ALTXT.d: Text string giving the engineering interpretation of the raw value in PAS_ALVAL (the alias). Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.

PCDF_DESC.d: Textual description of the element. The ICD states that it is used for fixed areas only (header parameters are described by PCPC_DESC).

PCDF_TYPE.d: Type of the header element, which determines where its value comes from at encoding time. A fixed area takes its value from PCDF_VALUE. PCDF_BIT.d: Bit offset of the element counted from the first bit of the whole packet, as an unsigned number of bits. It is part of the table key together with PCDF_TCNAME.

PCF_NAME.d: Alphanumeric name that uniquely identifies the monitoring parameter; it is the key used by every other table that refers to a monitoring parameter. Because the Operations Language (OL) recognises the nature of a component from its leading characters, no parameter name may start with 'VAR', 'GVAR' or '$'. For deduced telemetry parameters (PCF_PTC = 11) it names the telemetry parameter

Depending on the category the value must match TXF_NUMBR (PCF_CATEG = 'S') or CAF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT (PCF_CATEG = 'N') of an existing textual, numerical, polynom

The number of parameters that can be status-consistency checked is limited by the maximum size of the SCOS-2000 packet holding the snapshot of

PCF_DECIM.d: Number of decimal places used when displaying real values of the parameter.

PIC_PI1_OFF.d: Offset in bytes of the first additional identification field, counted from the start of the TM source packet (the start of the SCOS-2000 packet body). Set to -1 when no additional identification field is needed for this type/subtype combination.

PIC_PI1_WID.d: Width of the first additional identification field in bits.

PIC_PI2_OFF.d: Offset in bytes of the second additional identification field, if any, counted from the start of the TM source packet (start of the SCOS-2000 packet body). Set to -1 when the second field is not relevant.

PIC_PI2_WID.d: Width of the second additional identification field in bits.

PIC_APID.d: APID of the TM source packet to which this record is restricted. If the field is omitted or blank, no APID is specified and the record applies to all APIDs of this type/subtype; the import default 99999 stands for 'any APID'. Part of the table key since ICD 7.0.

PID_TYPE.d: PUS service type of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. Zero means that the packet has no specific type, e.g. it has no PUS data field header.

PID_STYPE.d: PUS service subtype of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. Zero means that the packet has no specific subtype (e.g. no PUS data field header).

PID_APID.d: Application process identifier of the TM source packet: 0 to 2047 for source packets generated by the spacecraft, 2048 to 65535 for any other SCOS-2000 TM packet, such as packets generated by SCOS-2000 applications or by other control domains (e.g. SCOE equipment).

PID_PI1_VAL.d: Value of the first additional identification field (for example a structure ID or task ID), used together with APID, type and subtype to identify the packet structure; where and how wide the field is comes from pic. Unsigned integer from 0 to 2^31-1. Enter 0 when pic is not used for the packet, because the packetiser then searches pid with PI1 = 0 and PI2 = 0.

PID_PI2_VAL.d: Value of the second additional identification field (for example a function ID), used together with APID, type, subtype and PI1 to identify the packet structure. Unsigned integer from 0 to 2^31-1; enter 0 when pic is not used.

PID_SPID.d: SCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Number (SCOS-2000 Packet ID, SPID). It uniquely identifies the structure of fixed TM packets described in plf and is the identifier used by tpcf, grpk and the archive; in releases up to S2K-R5 it also selected the history file in which the packet was archived. Unsigned integer from 1 to 2^32-1 (zero not allowed).

PID_DESCR.d: Textual description of the telemetry packet. When the packet triggers a SCOS-2000 event packet (PID_EVENT not 'N'), the packetiser uses this text as the event message.

PID_UNIT.d: On-board subsystem, intended for grouping packets for filtering (future extension). Grey and italic row in the ICD: not used and not currently supported by SCOS-2000.

PID_TPSD.d: SCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Structure Definition, used only by the Variable Packets Display application. Set it to -1 for packets not described in vpd; otherwise give the structure identifier, an unsigned integer from 1 to 2^31-1 (zero not allowed), that VPD_TPSD uses. The TPSD of packets already in the archive must not be changed, or archived packets will be reprocessed incorrectly with a new data

PID_DFHSIZE.d: Start reference, in octets from the end of the SCOS-2000 packet header, for interpreting variable packets with vpd. With the SCOS-2000 packetiser the whole source packet is stored in the SCOS-2000 packet body, so the reference is the start of the source packet header plus this number of bytes, typically the source packet header plus the PUS data field header. Irrelevant for fixed packets (PID_TPSD

PID_TIME.d: Whether the TM source packet contains a packet generation time field.

PID_INTER.d: Generation interval of periodic TM packets in milliseconds. SCOS-2000 uses it, plus a global margin, to decide when the parameter samples of a periodic packet expire, i.e. become invalid because no new packet arrived (pcf remark, p. 40). Must be left null for non-periodic packets.

PID_VALID.d: Whether this key combination is valid. It selects which SPID to use when several records share the same key. At import, if several records with the same key are flagged 'Y', only the last one stays valid and the others are forced to 'N'.

PID_CHECK.d: Whether the TM source packet carries a Packet Error Control field (checksum) and whether and how the packetiser checks it on reception. Missions may add options for other checksum algorithms.

PID_EVENT.d: Whether the packetiser generates a SCOS-2000 event packet when this source packet is received, and with which severity, e.g. to alert operators to anomaly reports. The event message text is PID_DESCR.

PID_EVID.d: Event number used as event ID of the generated SCOS-2000 event packet; the full event ID is 'TPKT_OBE::nnnn' with nnnn this value. A specific ID makes it possible to control the recipients of the event or trigger actions on reception. To avoid clashes with events of other SCOS-2000 applications (which use 5-digit numbers from 10000), values between 1 and 9999 are suggested. Optional; relevant only

PLF_NAME.d: Name of the monitoring parameter to be extracted; must match PCF_NAME.

PLF_SPID.d: SCOS-2000 Packet ID of the packet from which the parameter values are extracted; a positive integer matching PID_SPID.

PLF_OFFBY.d: Byte offset of the first occurrence of the parameter, counted from the end of the SCOS-2000 TM header. With the SCOS-2000 telemetry packetiser this coincides with the start of the TM source packet header. Integer starting from 0 (negative values not allowed).

PLF_OFFBI.d: Bit number, within the byte given by PLF_OFFBY, of the first bit of the first occurrence; bit 0 is the leftmost (most significant) bit of the byte. Integer from 0 to 7.

PLF_NBOCC.d: Number of occurrences of the parameter in the packet, from 1 to 9999. Use 1 for parameters that are not super-commutated.

PLF_LGOCC.d: Distance in bits between the starts of two consecutive occurrences of a super-commutated parameter, from 0 to 32767. Irrelevant when PLF_NBOCC = 1.

PLF_TIME.d: Time offset in milliseconds of the first occurrence relative to the packet time, used to adjust the time stamp of the extracted sample (for super-commutated and non-commutated parameters alike). Integer from -4080000 to 4080000. Together with PLF_TDOCC it is used by graphic displays to plot super-commutated samples and to show sample times on scrolling displays and printouts (Note 1, p. 98).

PLF_TDOCC.d: Time delay in milliseconds between two consecutive occurrences of a super-commutated parameter, from 1 to 4080000. Irrelevant when PLF_NBOCC = 1. Since ICD 6.1 the default is 1 and 0 is not an allowed value.

PPC_NUMBE.d: Name of the printout proforma; must match PPF_NUMBE of the corresponding printout. Part of the key.

PPC_POS.d: Position of the parameter in the printout. Part of the key.

PPC_NAME.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) printed in the printout.

PPC_FORM.d: Format used to print the parameter values. B, O and H apply only to raw values of unsigned integer parameters; N prints the engineering value for calibrated parameters, otherwise raw decimal.

PPF_NUMBE.d: Name of the printout proforma: alphanumeric string of up to 4 characters that uniquely identifies it. Referenced by ppc.PPC_NUMBE.

PPF_HEAD.d: Header printed on the top line of each printed page.

PPF_NBPR.d: Number of parameters to be printed, integer 1 to 32. Must equal the number of ppc records for this printout. Not marked mandatory in the ICD.

PRF_NUMBR.d: Alphanumeric name uniquely identifying the range set; referenced by CPC_PRFREF, CSP_PRFREF and PRV_NUMBR.

PRF_DESCR.d: Textual description of the range set.

PRF_INTER.d: Representation in which the limits PRV_MINVAL and PRV_MAXVAL of this set are written.

PRF_DSPFMT.d: Representation type of the limit values in PRV, whose value formats are given in Appendix A. It must be compatible with the parameters using the set: with their PTC when PRF_INTER=R, and with their DISPFMT when PRF_INTER=E or for time parameters.

PRF_RADIX.d: Radix of the limit values in PRV; only applicable for unsigned integers (PRF_DSPFMT=U). It may differ from the radix (CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX) of the parameters using the set.

PRF_NRANGE.d: Number of PRV records defined for this set. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

PRF_UNIT.d: Engineering unit mnemonic, for consistency checking against the unit (CPC_UNIT/CSP_UNIT) of the parameters using the set. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

PRV_NUMBR.d: Name (PRF_NUMBR) of the range set to which this allowed value or range belongs.

PRV_MINVAL.d: Low limit of the range, or the single allowed value if PRV_MAXVAL is empty. Written in a format compatible with PRF_DSPFMT (and PRF_RADIX for unsigned integers). Part of the key. Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.

PRV_MAXVAL.d: High limit of the range. Empty means that PRV_MINVAL is a discrete allowed value. Written in a format compatible with PRF_DSPFMT (and PRF_RADIX for unsigned integers).

PSM_NAME.d: Name of the task, a command (CCF_CNAME) or a sequence (CSF_NAME), to which the parameter set in PSM_PARSET is attached. Part of the key.

PSM_TYPE.d: Type of the task the parameter set is attached to. Part of the key.

PSM_PARSET.d: Name of the parameter set (PST_NAME) attached to this task. Part of the key.

PST_NAME.d: Unique name of the parameter set. Referenced by psv.PSV_NAME, cps.CPS_NAME, pvs.PVS_PSID and psm.PSM_PARSET.

PST_DESCR.d: Text description of the parameter set.

PSV_NAME.d: Name of the parameter set (PST_NAME) this value set belongs to. Mandatory but not part of the key.

PSV_PVSID.d: Unique name of the parameter value set; the table key. Referenced by pvs.PVS_ID, ccf.CCF_DEFSET, csf.CSF_DEFSET and sdf.SDF_VALSET.

PSV_DESCR.d: Text description of the parameter value set.

PTV_CNAME.d: Name of the command (CCF_CNAME) to which this validation check applies.

PTV_PARNAM.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) tested by the check. It must have a numerical raw representation (not a string or time) and must be processed by the telemetry model library, i.e. be a TM parameter appearing in PLF or a synthetic parameter of any type.

PTV_INTER.d: Representation in which the expected value PTV_VAL is written.

PTV_VAL.d: Value that the validation parameter must equal for the check to pass. It is written raw unless PTV_INTER=E: raw values in decimal, compatible with the parameter type (PCF_PTC); engineering values in the parameter's engineering representation (ASCII for textually calibrated parameters, PCF_CATEG=S, or the CAF_ENGFMT of the numeric calibration).

PVS_ID.d: Name of the parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) this record belongs to. Part of the key.

PVS_PSID.d: Name of the parameter set (PST_NAME) the value set belongs to.

PVS_PNAME.d: Name of the command parameter (CDF_PNAME) or sequence parameter (CSP_FPNAME) whose value is given in PVS_VALS. If two sequence parameters, or a command parameter and a sequence parameter, have the same name and are used in parameter sets, they must have the same raw and engineering formats: the same CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC and the same CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT.

PVS_INTER.d: Representation of the value in PVS_VALS.

PVS_VALS.d: Value for the parameter named in PVS_PNAME, in raw form unless PVS_INTER = 'E'. Raw values follow the parameter type (CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC) and, for unsigned integers, the radix (CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX). Engineering values follow the engineering representation (CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT). No fixed size: the maximum length depends on the maximum allowed command size (§3.3.3.2). May be left Null, in which cas

PVS_BIT.d: Unique identification of the parameter within the set: bit offset in the command (CDF_BIT) for command parameters, position (CSP_FPNUM) for sequence parameters. Part of the key.

COL1.d: Inferred: short name of the file attribute/category (PLAIN, OBCP, DEL, IMM, PAYLOAD, INVALID, OTHER). Unique.

COL2.d: Inferred: one-letter code of the category: N (PLAIN, PAYLOAD, INVALID, OTHER), O (OBCP), D (DEL), I (IMM). Exact meaning not determinable.

COL3.d: Inferred: numeric code of the category (PLAIN 0, OBCP 1, DEL 2, IMM 3, PAYLOAD 4, INVALID 5, OTHER 6). Always equal to COL4.

COL4.d: Inferred: second numeric code, identical to COL3 in all rows (perhaps a ground and an on-board value that happen to coincide).

COL5.d: Inferred: display or class name; equals COL1 except for PLAIN, whose value is PAYLOAD.

COL6.d: Inferred: human-readable description (e.g. 'DELAYED TC', 'IMMEDIATE TC', 'PAYLOAD CONTEXT').

COL1.d: Inferred: short partition name (TCFA, OBCA, SYSA, SPRA, TCFB, OBCB, SYSB, SPRB, CSWA, OBCS, CSWB). Unique; referenced by s13t.COL7.

COL2.d: Inferred: partition class. M for OMM TC-file, OBCP and spare partitions, B for the OMM system-file partitions, N for the SGM-EEPROM partitions. Meaning of the letters not determinable.

COL3.d: Inferred: on-board partition identifier (161-164, 177-180, 193-195), equal to the raw values of textual calibration CCDT0192TX ('Partition').

COL4.d: Inferred: second copy of the partition identifier; equal to COL3 in all rows.

COL5.d: Inferred: partition label; equal to COL1 in all rows.

COL6.d: Inferred: description of the partition, e.g. 'OMM TC Files (A)', 'SGM-EEPROM CSW TC Files (B)'.

COL1.d: Inferred: file type name (UNKNOWN, OBCP, SCOS0..SCOS3, CSF0..CSF3, PLAIN, ALL). Unique.

COL2.d: Inferred: one-letter code; C for ten concrete types, W for PLAIN and ALL. Meaning not determinable (W possibly 'wildcard', inference).

COL3.d: Inferred: numeric file type code (UNKNOWN -2, OBCP -1, SCOS0-3 0-3, CSF1 4, CSF2 5, CSF3 6, CSF0 7, PLAIN 8, ALL 9).

COL4.d: Inferred: format or converter used for the content (UNKNOWN, OBCP, CSF0-CSF3, BINARY); in 11 of 12 rows the value is itself a COL1 value of this table.

COL5.d: Inferred: description, e.g. 'SCOS stack file', 'Mixed TC sequence (CSF type 0)', 'Backup MTL (CSF type 3)'.

COL6.d: Inferred: file attribute name from s13a; filled only for UNKNOWN (OTHER) and OBCP (OBCP).

COL7.d: Inferred: default destination partition short name from s13p (SYSA, OBCA, TCFA); filled in 6 of 12 rows.

SDF_SQNAME.d: Name of the sequence (CSF_NAME) containing the element that owns this parameter.

SDF_ENTRY.d: Entry number (CSS_ENTRY) of the sequence element owning the parameter; it must designate an element of type command or sequence (CSS_TYPE C or S).

SDF_ELEMID.d: Name of the sequence element (CSS_ELEMID) owning the parameter, i.e. the command or nested sequence name.

SDF_POS.d: Position of the parameter: for a command element, the bit offset of the parameter in the command (CDF_BIT); for a nested sequence, the formal parameter number in that sequence (CSP_FPNUM). For commands with group repeaters it is the bit offset after expansion of the groups; if this differs from CDF_BIT, the original CDF_BIT must be given in SDF_REPPOS. Part of the key.

SDF_PNAME.d: Name of the element parameter: the editable command parameter (CDF_PNAME with CDF_ELTYPE=E) for a command element, or the formal parameter name (CSP_FPNAME) of the nested sequence. It is part of the key (the ICD stresses this for commands whose CDF_GRPSIZE is non-zero).

SDF_FTYPE.d: Whether the parameter value may still be modified after the sequence has been loaded on the stack. If the parameter is mapped to a formal parameter, its value can only be set (through the formal parameter) before loading.

SDF_VTYPE.d: Source of the parameter value and interpretation of SDF_VALUE.

SDF_VALUE.d: Value of the element parameter; its maximum length depends on the maximum command size. With VTYPE R or E it is written in the appropriate representation (raw compatible with CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC and CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX; engineering compatible with CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT). With VTYPE R, a 'Command ID' parameter takes the name of a fully defaulted command (CCF_CNAME) and a 'Parameter ID' parameter the

SDF_VALSET.d: Name of the parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) providing the value; applicable, and then mandatory, only when SDF_VTYPE=P.

SDF_REPPOS.d: Repeated position of a command parameter: the original bit offset of the parameter in the command definition (CDF_BIT), allowing a parameter shifted by the expansion of repeated groups to be mapped back to its definition at import. Mandatory when SDF_POS differs from CDF_BIT because of group expansion, optional otherwise.

SPC_NUMBE.d: Name of the SCD; must match SPF_NUMBE of the corresponding display. Part of the key.

SPC_POS.d: Order of the entry within the scrolling display. Part of the key; the file is expected to be sorted by SPC_NUMBE and SPC_POS.

SPC_NAME.d: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) shown in the scrolling display.

SPC_UPDT.d: Controls how the parameter is updated: by scrolling onto a new line or by overwriting the old value with the new one.

SPC_MODE.d: Controls whether the Telemetry Desktop option governing the display of invalid values applies. Unlike DPC_MODE (Y/N, default Y), the 'apply the option' value is a space.

SPC_FORM.d: Format used to display the value. B, O and H apply only to raw values of unsigned integer parameters; N shows the engineering value for calibrated parameters, otherwise raw decimal.

SPC_BACK.d: Background colour of the parameter field.

SPC_FORE.d: Foreground colour of the parameter field.

SPF_NUMBE.d: Name of the Scrolling Display (SCD): alphanumeric string that uniquely identifies it (the ICD misspells 'Scrolling' as 'Srolling'). Referenced by spc.SPC_NUMBE.

SPF_HEAD.d: Alphanumeric header shown on the top line of the display.

SPF_NPAR.d: Number of parameters in the display, integer 1 to 5. Must equal the number of spc records for this SCD (§3.3.2.7.6).

SPF_UPUN.d: Display update rate in seconds, integer 1 to 99. Provided for external applications that read the database; not used by SCOS-2000.

COL1.d: Placeholder column created for an empty file; no data, so no meaning can be inferred.
Inferred: SWA database item name (unique). Matches pcf.PCF_NAME (1,758), cpc.CPC_PNAME (428) and ccf.CCF_CNAME (184) of the SWA database; the rest match none.

COL2.d: Inferred: software name column, empty in all rows (by analogy with ASW_sw_para COL2).

COL3.d: Inferred: software/display name or description; 'a' is a placeholder in 2,463 rows; five rows hold 'x'.

TCP_ID.d: Unique identifier of the TC packet header definition. It is the value that commands quote in CCF_PKTID to select the header to be prepended when the command is encoded, and the value that PCDF records quote in PCDF_TCNAME to attach header elements to this header. Being the table key, a given name may appear only once; names are compared without regard to letter case and should not contain spaces (

TCP_DESC.d: Free-text description of the packet header (up to 24 characters). It is informative only and has no effect on encoding.

TPCF_SPID.d: SCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Number (SCOS-2000 Packet ID); unsigned integer that must match PID_SPID of the packet.

TPCF_NAME.d: Alphanumeric mnemonic of the telemetry packet, shown in the monitoring displays to identify the source packet of parameter values. If none is given, displays show the string 'None'.

TPCF_SIZE.d: Total length of the SCOS-2000 telemetry packet in bytes. Not imported into the run-time database and not used by any SCOS-2000 process (grey row); provided for mission-specific tools that generate history-file configuration. Recommended values: 0 for truly variable packets; for fixed packets the exact SCOS-2000 packet size, i.e. the SCOS-2000 TM header (64 bytes for header versions 0-3, 76 bytes f

TXF_NUMBR.d: Alphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the textual calibration; it is the value used in PCF_CURTX, CUR_SELECT and TXP_NUMBR.

TXF_DESCR.d: Free textual description of the textual calibration.

TXF_RAWFMT.d: Format of the raw values (TXP_FROM, TXP_TO) given in the txp records of this calibration. It must be compatible with the type of the parameters that use the calibration.

TXF_NALIAS.d: Number of records defined in txp for this textual calibration. Grey row in the ICD: informative, not used by SCOS-2000 processing.

TXP_NUMBR.d: Identifier of the textual calibration this entry belongs to; must match TXF_NUMBR of an existing txf record.

TXP_FROM.d: Lower bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.

TXP_TO.d: Upper bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.

TXP_ALTXT.d: Alphanumeric string (up to 14 characters) displayed as the engineering value for any raw value in the range TXP_FROM to TXP_TO.

VDF_NAME.d: Name of the database version: any alphanumeric string of up to 8 characters. It is the identifier shown by SCOS-2000 applications and used to check that artefacts such as saved stack files were produced with the same database version that is now loaded. When vdf.dat contains several records, the name in the last imported record wins.

VDF_COMMENT.d: Free-text comment associated with the database version (up to 32 characters). Together with VDF_NAME it forms the internal version description taken from the last imported record.

VDF_DOMAINID.d: Identifier of the SCOS-2000 domain to which the whole database belongs, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1. Storing it once here avoids a domain column in every table. If it is null, the current local domain identifier is assumed (section 3.3.1.1, p. 37). The importer cross-checks this value against the domain identifier passed to it as an input option.

VDF_RELEASE.d: Database release number, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1, used for database version management. Optional for backwards compatibility; a null value is treated as 0.

VDF_ISSUE.d: Database issue number within the release, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1, used for database version management. Optional for backwards compatibility; a null value is treated as 0.

VPD_TPSD.d: Telemetry Packet Structure Definition identifier; unsigned integer matching PID_TPSD of the packet(s) interpreted with this structure.

VPD_POS.d: Ordinal position of this parameter within the structure definition, used by database editors to deliver the records in the right order. Grey row in the ICD: the ordering is what matters to SCOS-2000, and the table is expected to be sorted by VPD_TPSD and VPD_POS.

VPD_NAME.d: Name of the parameter appearing at this position of the variable packet; must match PCF_NAME of the monitoring parameter to be processed and displayed.

VPD_GRPSIZE.d: Set only for parameters that are repeat counters (the PUS 'N') or for 'dummy' fixed-repetition parameters (see VPD_FIXREP). It gives the number of parameters in the group to be repeated: the group is formed by the next VPD_GRPSIZE records of the table. The VPD application supports nested structures, i.e. a repeat counter may itself be part of a repeated group.

VPD_FIXREP.d: Fixed repetition count for arrays of fixed size. A positive value is set on a counter parameter and gives the fixed number of repetitions of the group of VPD_GRPSIZE parameters that follows. Such parameters must be defined in pcf but are not present in the packet: they only declare the fixed array size.

VPD_CHOICE.d: Whether the value of this parameter selects the structure of the rest of the packet: if 'Y', the value read is used as a TPSD key to interpret the following entries, and the choice parameter must be the last one of its TPSD group. The row is in italics: per section 3.3.2.5.2 (p. 106), choice structures are not currently supported by the VPD application.

VPD_PIDREF.d: Whether the value of this field is an on-board parameter identifier (the PUS 'Parameter#'). If 'Y', the value is compared with PCF_PID values to find the SCOS-2000 name of the parameter, e.g. for the parameter-number column of a monitoring report.

VPD_DISDESC.d: Textual description of the parameter value, used in the displays to build the header line (column title).

VPD_WIDTH.d: Display width control: 0 hides the value; any number greater than 0 displays it with its full length.

VPD_JUSTIFY.d: Justification of the value field in the display.

VPD_NEWLINE.d: Whether the parameter is displayed or printed on a new line. 'Y' is allowed only for parameters that are not part of structures with repeated groups, since each repetition is automatically aligned on its own row. When set to 'Y', all parameters of the packet are displayed on separate lines.

VPD_DCHAR.d: What is displayed for the parameter. Relevant only for packets with a fixed number of parameters (no group repeater). In variable packets the value 2 may only be used for parameters with VPD_PIDREF = 'Y' to show the PCF_NAME and PCF_DESCR of the identified parameter; other parameters show only the value, their description being in the column header.

VPD_FORM.d: Display format of the parameter value.

VPD_OFFSET.d: Number of bits between the end of the previous parameter and the start of this one. A positive value leaves a gap, a negative value makes this parameter overlap bits of the previous one(s). Integer from -32768 to 32767.
